cards.d: An abbey is a house or group of houses where monks or nuns live.
cards.e: When the monk returned to the abbey, he went immediately to his bedroom.

cards.d: If something is abundant, then it is available in large quantities.
cards.e: Cakes, cookies, and candy were so abundant that the child was very happy.

cards.d: To adjoin something means to be next to or attached to something else.
cards.e: She can listen to her brother’s conversations because her room adjoins his.

cards.d: If something is ample, then it is enough or more than enough.
cards.e: There was an ample supply of oats to feed the horses.

cards.d: If a place is arid, then it is hot and dry and gets very little or no rain.
cards.e: Not many plants grow in the arid desert.

cards.d: A cathedral is an important and often large and beautifully built church.
cards.e: The large cathedral is full of people on Sunday mornings.

cards.d: To deprive someone of something means to not let them have it.
cards.e: Because the child was bad, she was deprived of her dessert after dinner.

cards.d: A drought is a long period of time in which little or no rain falls.
cards.e: After three months of drought, the vegetation and trees started dying.

cards.d: If someone is eligible, then they are permitted to do or have something.
cards.e: Only people who bought tickets were eligible to win a prize.

cards.d: To fast means to go without food or drink for a period of time.
cards.e: In her religion, they fast for five days and then have a big feast.

cards.d: To grumble means to complain.
cards.e: He grumbled about having to work late on Friday.

cards.d: If someone goes inland, they travel into the center of a country or land.
cards.e: The river curved inland near the campground.

cards.d: Moisture is small drops of water in the air or on a surface.
cards.e: If you breathe on a window, moisture from your breath collects on the glass.

cards.d: If something happens nonetheless, then it occurs despite some other thing.
cards.e: She tried to keep the dog out of the mud, but it got dirty nonetheless.

cards.d: An oath is a formal, often public, promise.
cards.e: Judges must take an oath to be fair to everyone in court.

cards.d: A prairie is a large flat area of grassland.
cards.e: The prairie was perfect for a farm because there were hills and trees.

cards.d: If something is ragged, then it is old, torn, and falling apart.
cards.e: They could see his toes through the holes in his ragged shoes.

cards.d: If an area of land is rugged, then it is rocky and difficult to travel through.
cards.e: Their car couldn’t make it far along the rugged roads.

cards.d: If something is scarce, then it is in a very small amount.
cards.e: When gasoline was scarce, we rode our bikes, instead of driving, to school.

cards.d: To speculate means to guess about something.
cards.e: My sister looked at the sky and speculated that it would rain tomorrow.
